payload.body:
You notice quickly who actually has power, and official titles matter less to you than who can change the outcome. Wherever your contribution is visible, you pay attention to who controls the money, access, information, exceptions, or final decision.

You rarely take the official explanation at face value. You notice which rules are enforced, which ones quietly disappear for certain people, who gets heard without having to ask twice, and what the structure actually rewards even when its public explanation says something different.

The challenge is that power can become too central to the way you measure progress. You may keep trying to prove yourself to someone whose approval carries more weight than it should, make yourself indispensable because being needed feels safer than being replaceable, or stay engaged with a structure because you want it to acknowledge what you can already see clearly.

Your relationship with ambition gets clearer when you ask what authority would actually change. More influence should give you more say over what gets built, protected, funded, ended, or made possible. If the title does not change what you can actually do, it may be giving you status without giving you much power.
